Split into three children: two comparator-accepted lemmas reused with identical frozen types, and one new analytic lemma. This makes the proof safer and reuses existing work.

The supplied proof has three parts.
- Step 3 derives spt Z ⊆ L from the fact that Z annihilates every test form whose tsupport misses the closed set L, using balls B_{ε/2}(p) that lie in the zero region. - Step 2's analytic core is the single new child iwl_cr_ci_ps_slice_integral_eq_zero. For η with tsupport η ∩ L = ∅ and any family φ satisfying the slice identity on [0, 1], each slice φ(s) vanishes on the open set N_s ⊇ B̄_R(0) ⊇ spt X. So X(φ(s)) = 0, and hence ∫_0^1 X(φ(s)) ds = 0. The child takes φ as data, so it depends only on the accepted vanish_off_support. That lemma is listed again as a reused sibling with its identical type, as in the accepted cone_im decomposition, so that the new child can declare the dependency. The child does not depend on slice_forms (iwl_cr_ci_slice_testForm), which is not yet accepted and so cannot be a child. slice_forms is already a declared prerequisite of the selected node and is used only in the parent assembly.
- Step 1 (L is compact and closed) is three lines of glue in the assembly.

subproblems.title: A current vanishing on test forms supported off a closed set K has support in K (reused accepted lemma)
subproblems.statement: Let P, q ∈ ℕ, V ⊆ ℝ^P open, K ⊆ ℝ^P closed, and Z ∈ D_q(V) (GeometricCurrentOn V q) with Z(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ D^q(V) whose tsupport is disjoint from K. Then spt Z ⊆ K. Here spt Z = Z.support = V ∖ zeroRegion(Z), and zeroRegion(Z) is the union of all open W ⊆ ℝ^P with closure W compact, closure W ⊆ V and Z(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ D^q(V) with tsupport ω ⊆ W (Simon Ch. 6, 2.11). (Reuse, with identical frozen Lean type, of the comparator-accepted declaration fiw_tb_ext_support_subset.)
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P q : ℕ) (V K : Set (Eucl P)) (Z : GeometricCurrentOn V q), IsOpen V → IsClosed K → (∀ ω : TestFormOn V q, Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) q)) K → Z ω = 0) → Z.support ⊆ K
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the accepted proof of the reused declaration fiw_tb_ext_support_subset (node root.flat_iff_weak-a1.total_boundedness-a1.extend-a1.support_subset-a1), reproduced verbatim after this Source paragraph (which replaces the original Source sentence naming that node's own parent steps); the frozen Lean type is identical, so the comparator-accepted declaration is reused. In the selected parent it is applied with P := P + 1, q := m + 1, V := univ (open) and K := L = Φ([0, 1] × B̄_R(0)) (closed, being compact).

Recall that Z.VanishesOn W means Z(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ D^q(V) with tsupport ω ⊆ W.

1. Let x ∈ spt Z, so x ∈ V and x ∉ zeroRegion(Z). Suppose, for a contradiction, that x ∉ K.
2. V ∖ K is open (V open, K closed; IsOpen.sdiff) and contains x. So there is ε > 0 with ball(x, ε) ⊆ V ∖ K (Metric.isOpen_iff). Put r := ε/2 > 0 and W := ball(x, r).
3. Properties of W.
   - W is open.
   - closure W ⊆ closedBall(x, r) (closure_ball_subset_closedBall). closedBall(x, r) is compact because ℝ^P is a proper space (isCompact_closedBall), and closure W is closed, so closure W is compact.
   - closedBall(x, r) ⊆ ball(x, ε) since r < ε (closedBall_subset_ball). Hence closure W ⊆ ball(x, ε) ⊆ V ∖ K ⊆ V.
4. Z.VanishesOn W. Let ω ∈ D^q(V) with tsupport ω ⊆ W. Since W ⊆ ball(x, ε) ⊆ ℝ^P ∖ K, tsupport ω is disjoint from K, so Z(ω) = 0 by hypothesis.
5. By steps 3–4, W is one of the sets whose union is zeroRegion(Z), and x ∈ W because r > 0. So x ∈ zeroRegion(Z), contradicting step 1. Hence x ∈ K, and spt Z ⊆ K. ∎

Reference Lean proof (kernel-checked in a scratch build importing GMT.Ch06.Submission, in the comparator's contract scope; sibling dependencies are referenced as Submission.X):
theorem Submission.fiw_tb_ext_support_subset : ∀ (P q : ℕ) (V K : Set (Eucl P)) (Z : GeometricCurrentOn V q), IsOpen V → IsClosed K → (∀ ω : TestFormOn V q, Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) q)) K → Z ω = 0) → Z.support ⊆ K := by
  intro P q V K Z hV hK hZ x hx
  by_contra hxK
  obtain ⟨hxV, hxz⟩ := hx
  obtain ⟨ε, hε, hball⟩ := Metric.isOpen_iff.mp (hV.sdiff hK) x ⟨hxV, hxK⟩
  apply hxz
  refine ⟨ball x (ε / 2), ⟨isOpen_ball, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩, mem_ball_self (half_pos hε)⟩
  · exact (isCompact_closedBall x (ε / 2)).of_isClosed_subset isClosed_closure
      closure_ball_subset_closedBall
  · exact (closure_ball_subset_closedBall.trans
      (closedBall_subset_ball (half_lt_self hε))).trans (hball.trans sdiff_subset)
  · intro ω hω
    apply hZ
    rw [Set.disjoint_left]
    intro y hy hyK
    exact (hball (ball_subset_ball (half_le_self hε.le) (hω hy))).2 hyK
proof_key_steps: For x ∈ spt Z ∖ K, V ∖ K is an open neighbourhood of x; choose ball(x, ε) ⊆ V ∖ K.
W := ball(x, ε/2) is open with compact closure ⊆ V. Every test form supported in W has support disjoint from K, so Z vanishes on W.
Hence x ∈ zeroRegion(Z), contradicting x ∈ spt Z.

subproblems.title: Currents annihilate test forms supported off their support (reused accepted lemma)
subproblems.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ, every set U ⊆ ℝ^P, every current T ∈ GeometricCurrentOn U n and every test form ω ∈ TestFormOn U n: if tsupport ω is disjoint from spt T = U ∖ zeroRegion(T), then T(ω) = 0. (Reuse, with identical frozen Lean type, of the comparator-accepted declaration isoperimetric_apply_eq_zero_of_disjoint_support.)
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (ω : TestFormOn U n), Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n)) T.support → T ω = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the accepted proof of the reused declaration isoperimetric_apply_eq_zero_of_disjoint_support (node root.isoperimetric-a1.vanish_off_support-a1), reproduced verbatim; the frozen Lean type is identical, so the comparator-accepted declaration is reused.

Notation. For T ∈ GeometricCurrentOn U n, `T.VanishesOn W` means T(η) = 0 for every η ∈ TestFormOn U n with tsupport η ⊆ W. Let 𝒲 be the family of all W ⊆ ℝ^P with W open, closure W compact, closure W ⊆ U and T.VanishesOn W. By definition T.zeroRegion = ⋃𝒲 and T.support = U ∖ T.zeroRegion.

1. Let K := tsupport ω. Since ω ∈ TestFormOn U n, ω is C^∞, has compact support (so K is compact, in particular closed) and K ⊆ U.
2. K ⊆ ⋃𝒲. Let x ∈ K. Then x ∈ U, and x ∉ T.support by the disjointness hypothesis, i.e. x ∉ U ∖ T.zeroRegion; hence x ∈ T.zeroRegion = ⋃𝒲.
3. Every member of 𝒲 is open, so by compactness of K there are finitely many W_1, …, W_r ∈ 𝒲 (r ≥ 0; r = 0 when K = ∅) with K ⊆ W_1 ∪ ⋯ ∪ W_r (e.g. `IsCompact.elim_finite_subcover_image`; it is convenient to index the cover by the resulting finite subfamily rather than by Fin r).
4. ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P), with the model with corners 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ^P), is a finite-dimensional, Hausdorff, σ-compact smooth manifold, and K is closed and covered by the open sets W_i (i ranging over the finite index set of step 3). Hence there is a smooth partition of unity on K subordinate to (W_i): C^∞ functions ψ_1, …, ψ_r : ℝ^P → [0, 1] with tsupport ψ_i ⊆ W_i for every i and Σ_i ψ_i(x) = 1 for every x ∈ K (Mathlib `SmoothPartitionOfUnity.exists_isSubordinate`; a real-valued `ContMDiff 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ^P) 𝓘(ℝ)` function of class C^∞ is `ContDiff ℝ ∞` by `contMDiff_iff_contDiff`).
5. For each i put η_i(x) := ψ_i(x) • ω(x). Then η_i is C^∞ (a C^∞ scalar function times a C^∞ form). If ω(x) = 0 or ψ_i(x) = 0 then η_i(x) = 0, so support η_i ⊆ support ω ∩ support ψ_i; taking closures, tsupport η_i ⊆ K ∩ tsupport ψ_i ⊆ U ∩ W_i. In particular η_i has compact support (closed subset of the compact K). Thus η_i ∈ TestFormOn U n and tsupport η_i ⊆ W_i.
6. Since W_i ∈ 𝒲, T vanishes on W_i, so T(η_i) = 0 for every i.
7. ω = Σ_i η_i in TestFormOn U n (checked pointwise). If x ∈ K, then Σ_i ψ_i(x) • ω(x) = (Σ_i ψ_i(x)) • ω(x) = ω(x). If x ∉ K, then x ∉ support ω, so ω(x) = 0 and every η_i(x) = 0. (If r = 0 then K = ∅, ω = 0 and both sides are 0.)
8. T acts ℝ-linearly on TestFormOn U n (T.toCurrent is a linear map), so by steps 6 and 7, T(ω) = Σ_i T(η_i) = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: tsupport ω is a compact subset of U disjoint from spt T, hence contained in the zero region, i.e. covered by the open sets W on which T vanishes.
Extract a finite subcover W_1, …, W_r of tsupport ω.
Take a smooth partition of unity ψ_1, …, ψ_r on tsupport ω subordinate to the W_i (Mathlib SmoothPartitionOfUnity.exists_isSubordinate).
Each ψ_i • ω is a test form in U with tsupport in W_i, so T(ψ_i • ω) = 0.
ω = Σ_i ψ_i • ω pointwise, so T(ω) = 0 by linearity.

subproblems.title: Slices of a form supported off Φ([0,1] × B̄_R(0)) are annihilated by X, so ∫_0^1 X(φ(s)) ds = 0
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ and R ∈ ℝ. For s ∈ ℝ and x ∈ ℝ^P let Φ(s, x) := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P + 1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons s (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ x)) ∈ ℝ^{P+1} (so Φ(s, x)_0 = s and Φ(s, x)_{j+1} = x_j), let e_0 := EuclideanSpace.single 0 1 ∈ ℝ^{P+1}, ι(w) := Φ(0, w) for w ∈ ℝ^P, and L := {Φ(p.1, p.2) : p ∈ [0, 1] × B̄_R(0)} ⊆ ℝ^{P+1}. Let X ∈ D_m(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ m) with spt X ⊆ B̄_R(0), let η ∈ D^{m+1}(ℝ^{P+1}) (TestFormOn univ (m + 1)) with tsupport η disjoint from L, and let φ : ℝ → D^m(ℝ^P) (TestFormOn univ m) satisfy φ(s)(x)(v) = η(Φ(s, x))(e_0, ι(v_1), …, ι(v_m)) for all s ∈ [0, 1], x ∈ ℝ^P and v ∈ (ℝ^P)^m. Then the interval integral ∫_0^1 X(φ(s)) ds equals 0.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (R : ℝ) (X : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Eucl P)) m) (η : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Eucl (P + 1))) (m + 1)) (φ : ℝ → TestFormOn (univ : Set (Eucl P)) m), X.support ⊆ closedBall 0 R → Disjoint (tsupport (η : DifferentialForm (Eucl (P + 1)) (m + 1))) ((fun p : ℝ × Eucl P => (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P + 1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons p.1 (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ p.2))) '' (Icc (0 : ℝ) 1 ×ˢ closedBall (0 : Eucl P) R)) → (∀ s ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, ∀ (x : Eucl P) (v : Fin m → Eucl P), (φ s : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) m) x v = (η : DifferentialForm (Eucl (P + 1)) (m + 1)) ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P + 1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons s (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ x))) (Fin.cons (EuclideanSpace.single 0 1) fun i => (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P + 1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons 0 (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ (v i))))) → ∫ s in (0 : ℝ)..1, X (φ s) = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Step 2 ("Forms supported off L are annihilated") of the supplied proof of the selected theorem iwl_cr_ci_product_support, specialized: the slice family φ is given as data (in the selected theorem it is produced by slice_forms) and only the vanishing of ∫_0^1 X(φ(s)) ds is proved; the product identity (Prod) is not used here.

Notation (as in the parent proof): E := ℝ^P = Eucl P and E′ := ℝ^{P+1} = Eucl (P + 1); Φ(s, x) := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P + 1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons s (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ x)) ∈ E′ for s ∈ ℝ, x ∈ E; e_0 := EuclideanSpace.single 0 1 ∈ E′; ι(w) := Φ(0, w) for w ∈ E; D^k(E) := TestFormOn univ k and D_k(E) := GeometricCurrentOn univ k; L := {Φ(p.1, p.2) : p ∈ [0, 1] × B̄_R(0)}, the image of Icc 0 1 ×ˢ closedBall 0 R under p ↦ Φ(p.1, p.2). Hypotheses: (H1) spt X ⊆ B̄_R(0); (H2) tsupport η and L are disjoint; (H3) φ(s)(x)(v) = η(Φ(s, x))(Fin.cons e_0 (fun i => ι(v i))) for all s ∈ [0, 1], x ∈ E and v : Fin m → E. (If R < 0 then B̄_R(0) = ∅ and L = ∅; the argument below applies verbatim.)

1. (Continuity of Φ(s, ·).) Fix s ∈ ℝ. The map x ↦ Φ(s, x) is continuous: EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ and (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P + 1)) ℝ).symm are continuous linear equivalences, and w ↦ Fin.cons s w from Fin P → ℝ to Fin (P + 1) → ℝ is continuous (Continuous.finCons applied to the constant map s and the identity: coordinate 0 is the constant s and coordinate j + 1 is w_j).
2. (The sets C_s and N_s.) Fix s ∈ [0, 1] and put C_s := {x ∈ E : Φ(s, x) ∈ tsupport η} and N_s := E ∖ C_s = {x ∈ E : Φ(s, x) ∉ tsupport η}. Since tsupport η is closed (isClosed_tsupport), C_s is closed as the preimage of a closed set under the continuous map of step 1; hence N_s is open.
3. (B̄_R(0) ⊆ N_s.) Let x ∈ E with ‖x‖ ≤ R, i.e. x ∈ closedBall 0 R. Then (s, x) ∈ [0, 1] × B̄_R(0), so Φ(s, x) ∈ L. By (H2), Φ(s, x) ∉ tsupport η, i.e. x ∈ N_s.
4. (φ(s) vanishes on N_s, hence tsupport φ(s) ⊆ C_s.) Let x ∈ N_s. Then Φ(s, x) ∉ tsupport η, so η(Φ(s, x)) = 0 as a covector (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport). By (H3), which applies because s ∈ [0, 1], for every v : Fin m → E we get φ(s)(x)(v) = η(Φ(s, x))(Fin.cons e_0 (fun i => ι(v i))) = 0, so φ(s)(x) = 0 as a continuous alternating map (extensionality). Thus support φ(s) ⊆ C_s, and since C_s is closed (step 2), tsupport φ(s) = closure (support φ(s)) ⊆ C_s (closure_minimal).
5. (X(φ(s)) = 0.) Suppose x ∈ tsupport φ(s) and x ∈ spt X. By (H1), x ∈ B̄_R(0), so x ∈ N_s by step 3; but x ∈ C_s by step 4, contradicting N_s = E ∖ C_s. Hence tsupport φ(s) and spt X are disjoint, and vanish_off_support (applied with P, n := m, U := univ, T := X, ω := φ(s)) gives X(φ(s)) = 0.
6. (The integral vanishes.) By step 5, X(φ(s)) = 0 for every s ∈ [0, 1], and uIcc 0 1 = [0, 1] because 0 ≤ 1 (uIcc_of_le). So the integrands s ↦ X(φ(s)) and s ↦ 0 agree on uIcc 0 1, and intervalIntegral.integral_congr gives ∫_0^1 X(φ(s)) ds = ∫_0^1 0 ds = 0 (intervalIntegral.integral_zero). ∎
proof_key_steps: For fixed s, x ↦ Φ(s, x) is continuous, so C_s = {x : Φ(s, x) ∈ tsupport η} is closed and N_s = E ∖ C_s is open.
For s ∈ [0, 1], B̄_R(0) ⊆ N_s, because Φ(s, x) ∈ L whenever ‖x‖ ≤ R and tsupport η misses L.
By the slice identity and η = 0 off tsupport η, φ(s) vanishes on N_s, so tsupport φ(s) ⊆ C_s (closure_minimal).
spt X ⊆ B̄_R(0) ⊆ N_s, so tsupport φ(s) is disjoint from spt X and X(φ(s)) = 0 by vanish_off_support.
The integrand vanishes on uIcc 0 1 = [0, 1], so ∫_0^1 X(φ(s)) ds = 0 by intervalIntegral.integral_congr.
